objectives: Students will recognize the unique characteristics of oral presentations in digital environments.
Students will develop argumentation and organizational strategies for speeches delivered in digital environments.
Students will develop abilities to listen critically to speeches delivered in digital environments.
Students will critique the strategies of contemporary presentations in digital environments.
Students will practice delivery of diverse oral presentation techniques in digital environments.
Students will consider the ethical implications of communicating in digital environments.
topics: Foundations of oral presentation II.
The ethics of digital communication III.
Video resumes IV.
Interviewing through digital video V.
Conducting a meeting or seminar through online conferencing VI.
Developing an individual presentation product VII.
Speech anxiety in digital settings VIII.
Language choices for speeches delivered in digital settings

objectives: By the end of this course, students will be able to explain the logic, concepts, and process of social science research as it applies to communication.
By the end of this course, students will be able to locate, summarize, and critically evaluate published research that examines communication in various contexts.
By the end of this course, students will be able to construct hypotheses about communication processes and design quantitative surveys to test them.
By the end of this course, students will be able to compose a quantitative-methods research proposal to assess the influence and outcomes of communication.
topics: Introduction to research in communication and the research process.
The logic, concepts, and process of social science research as it applies to communication.
Constructing hypotheses about communication processes and designing quantitative surveys to test them.
The final group project: A quantitative-methods research proposal to assess the influence and outcomes of communication.
